correctness.rationale: Kakutani representation places any real AM-space lattice-isometrically as a closed sublattice of some \(C(K)\). For a fixed center \(w\), choose a point where its sup norm is attained. Pairwise disjointness means at most one sequence element is nonzero there, so the internal metric functional is nonnegative on all but at most one term. Pointwise closure then shows the same two-negative-values obstruction for every metric functional, proving d-weak nullity. Scaling a standard infinite disjoint positive sequence gives arbitrary norm profiles. Convex norm-continuity makes the metric-functional topology no finer than the weak topology; an unbounded d-weakly null sequence separates them in infinite dimension, while finite-dimensional AM-spaces reduce to finite \(\ell_\infty\) and the coordinate functionals arise as metric-functional limits.
residual_risks: The claim is specific to real AM-spaces and does not extend to arbitrary Banach lattices by this argument.

originality.rationale: A published C(K) result already proves arbitrary-profile disjoint d-weak null sequences and the finite/infinite topology dichotomy for full continuous-function spaces. The AM-space theorem is not a formal restriction of that result: a general AM-space is only a closed lattice subspace of \(C(K)\), and metric functionals of an isometric subspace need not be restrictions of ambient metric functionals. The assigned proof reruns the internal-center argument inside the represented sublattice and strengthens it to every pairwise disjoint sequence. Current searches found no prior abstract-AM formulation or theorem implying this subspace transfer.
